user_intent: Harden governance-core detection and command-layer gates after real-provider probes exposed gaps in proposal detection and approval/start enforcement.
title: Harden governance-core protected surfaces and proposal approval gates
description: Real-provider adversarial probes found two governance weaknesses: changes to abyss_cli/changeset.py executor allowlists were not detected as permission-boundary governance-core scope, and evolution approve/workflow start did not hard-block proposals already marked requires_meta_governance or implementation_allowed=false. This request records an owner-requested meta iteration to close both gaps without weakening Owner, Harness, or apply gates.
expected_artifacts: Detect abyss_cli/changeset.py as a permission-boundary governance-core surface
Reject ordinary evolution approve for governance-core proposals that require meta-governance
Reject workflow creation for governance-core proposals that require meta-governance or are not implementation_allowed
Regression tests for F1 and F2

request_fields.activation_policy: delayed; candidate code is reviewable evidence in this cycle and does not retroactively approve, apply, or activate any governance-core change outside the normal gates
request_fields.affected_governance_surface: Governance-core scope detection, permission-boundary protected surface definitions, evolution proposal approval command gate, and workflow creation command gate.
request_fields.current_problem: F1: permission_boundaries protects rules/capabilities.yaml and rules/policy.yaml but misses abyss_cli/changeset.py, where executor allowlists and blocklists live. F2: proposals marked requires_meta_governance and implementation_allowed=false can still be approved by evolution approve and started as workflows, making the marker advisory rather than a hard command-layer gate.
request_fields.old_rule_review: Prior accepted rules require governance-core mutations to go through meta-governance, old-rule review, explicit Owner approval, risk assessment, rollback plan, validation plan, and delayed activation. Ordinary self-evolution must not self-approve or same-cycle activate governance-core changes.
request_fields.owner_authority_impact: No Owner authority is delegated or reduced. The change strengthens command-layer refusal for governance-core proposals unless an explicit meta-governance route is used, and it does not approve, apply, start, or activate any specific proposal by itself.
request_fields.risk_assessment: Medium-to-high governance safety fix. The change makes detection and command gates stricter, which may block ordinary approve/start attempts for governance-core proposals until they are routed through explicit meta-governance. This is intended; it prevents relying on provider judgment as the final safety layer.
request_fields.rollback_plan: Revert the added protected surface entry for abyss_cli/changeset.py, remove the evolution/workflow governance-core blocking helpers, and remove the regression tests. Existing non-governance proposal approval/start behavior should remain unchanged.
request_fields.validation_plan: Run targeted governance-core gate tests, relevant edit-plan tests, full pytest, and abyss_cli check. Confirm changeset.py allowlist requests are detected, ordinary approve is blocked for governance-core proposals, and workflow start cannot bypass the block.
request_fields.proposed_change: Add abyss_cli/changeset.py to permission_boundaries. Add command-layer hard gates so ordinary evolution approve and workflow creation reject proposals with governance_core_detection.requires_meta_governance unless a future explicit meta-governance approval path is implemented. Preserve implementation_allowed checks.

notes: This is the record-before-mutation step for the owner-reported F1/F2 findings from real-provider adversarial testing.
